clue.text: Evaluate animals before start of show

indicators.note: before tells you the donkeys are written ahead of the single letter that follows

parts.note: asses are donkeys, so a plural animal word

indicators.note: start of asks for only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A judge looks the livestock over ahead of the opening of an agricultural show.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight synonym: to evaluate something is to judge or appraise its worth.

clue.text: A punter's fellow criminals?

parts.note: a punter is someone who places bets, a better; the possessive gives better's

explanation.surface: The partners in crime of a man who gambles.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a punter is a gambler. The question mark admits the definition is loose: those who abet a crime are accomplices.
explanation.definitionFit: People who abet a crime are accomplices, the partners of the one who commits it.

clue.text: Sarah's leading a dance

indicators.note: leading says the pet name comes first, in front of the letter that follows

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of Sarah, so Sarah's is Sal's

explanation.surface: Sarah is out in front of a line of dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a lively Latin American dance.

clue.text: Walker stirred into action

indicators.note: putting something into action sets it moving, so the letters before it are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A keen hiker is roused and gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' looks like the anagram signal but it is the fodder; 'into action' is what rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who walks with long steps is one kind of walker.

clue.text: Society makes fun of countryfolks' garb?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society, as in RSPCA
to make fun of someone is to mock them, so makes fun of is mocks

explanation.surface: Fashionable people laugh at what rural people wear.
explanation.definitionFit: These loose linen overgarments were the traditional working dress of English farm labourers and shepherds.

clue.text: Drink? Harm comes with one can being imbibed

indicators.note: something imbibed is taken in, so the container word is swallowed by the letters around it
comes with sets the single letter beside the word for harm

parts.note: to mar something is to harm or spoil it
I is the Roman numeral for one
a can of food is a tin in British English

explanation.surface: A warning that even a single tin of drink does damage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'one can' as a single tin of drink, but the two words are separate pieces, and 'being imbibed' is a swallowing instruction, not a description of drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a brand of vermouth and a gin cocktail.

clue.text: Opposing research establishment, journalist is worried

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
CERN is the European particle physics laboratory near Geneva
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor, a senior journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter who is against a laboratory feels anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight synonym: anxious or troubled about something.

clue.text: See detective hustle about

indicators.note: about suggests the letters before it are thrown around into a different order

explanation.surface: Watch a private eye bustling around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of 'hustle'; 'See' only introduces the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal synonym for an investigator, from the word for a bloodhound.

clue.text: Gentlemanly, offering source of water and food, we hear

parts.note: a well is a shaft sunk to draw water

indicators.note: we hear says the word for food is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: bread is a staple food

explanation.surface: A courteous host provides drink and something to eat, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A near-synonym: brought up with good manners, as a gentleman is supposed to be.

clue.text: Girl's father venting his spleen, being abusive

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana, so girl's is Di's
pa is an informal word for father
to vent your spleen is to pour out your anger, so he is raging

explanation.surface: A girl's dad loses his temper and hurls insults.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking of someone in a belittling, insulting way is being abusive about them.

clue.text: Call with hesitation someone who shouldn't be competing?

indicators.note: with tacks the sound of hesitation on after the word for call

parts.note: to call someone on the telephone is to ring them
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Nervously phoning an entrant who ought to be disqualified.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a horse or athlete fraudulently substituted in a contest, so one with no right to take part.

clue.text: What would bring some philosophers to Athens?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about what attracted thinkers to the ancient Greek capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the painted colonnade in Athens where Zeno taught, which gave the Stoics their name.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole question describes it: a covered colonnade in Athens where Zeno's school of thinkers gathered.

clue.text: Man facing two ways, sent out to get protesters

indicators.note: facing two ways says the man's name appears twice, once backwards and once forwards

parts.note: Sid is a man's name, short for Sidney
the same name Sid again, this time the right way round

indicators.note: out can mean astray or wrong, so the letters of the word before it are disordered

explanation.surface: A two-faced fellow is dispatched to round up demonstrators.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a two-faced man. 'facing two ways' really asks for a name written backwards and then forwards, and 'out' disorders the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: People who openly oppose official policy, as demonstrators do.

clue.text: Keeping quiet when having doubt

indicators.note: when having sets the musical letter alongside the word for doubt

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quiet
a reservation is a doubt that stops you agreeing fully

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent while unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping quiet' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Keeping' alone and 'quiet' is a piece of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a noun: the keeping of something is its maintenance in an unspoilt state.

clue.text: Time when, in short, pest could be destroyed

definitions.text: Time when, in short, pest could be destroyed

parts.words: Time when, in short, pest could be destroyed
parts.note: a time of year whose usual four-letter abbreviation is the letters of pest broken up and put in a new order

explanation.surface: The season at which, briefly put, vermin can be wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' points to the abbreviation SEPT, and 'pest could be destroyed' says PEST can be rearranged into it. The wordplay builds only the abbreviation, so the clue works as a riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle-like description: the ninth month, a period whose abbreviated name uses the letters of a word for vermin.

clue.text: Formal code of primitive army officer

parts.note: proto- is the prefix meaning first or primitive, as in prototype
Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army rank

explanation.surface: The strict rulebook of an uncivilised military commander.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the official rules of procedure and etiquette, especially in diplomacy.

clue.text: LSD operators organised documents for payment

indicators.note: organised says the letters before it have been arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Drug dealers set up the paperwork for getting paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges 'LSD operators'. LSD looks like the drug, but it was also the British shorthand for pounds, shillings and pence, which suits these slips bought at a post office to send money.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain these are slips bought at a post office and sent by mail to pay a named person.

clue.text: First sign of sun and furry animal will get to brighten up

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a marten is a weasel-like mammal valued for its fur

explanation.surface: Dawn breaks and a small creature appears, cheering the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to make something neater and more cheerful in appearance.

clue.text: Plan not permitted, leading to row

indicators.note: leading to says the first word runs straight on into the second

parts.note: something that is out is ruled out, not allowed
a row of things is a line of them

explanation.surface: A scheme is refused permission, and an argument follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'row' to be a quarrel; here it is a row of things standing side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a sketch of the main points of a scheme.

clue.text: People who don't want certain food, say, put in vehicles

definitions.text: People who don't want certain food

indicators.note: put in places the short abbreviation inside the word for vehicles

parts.note: vans are goods vehicles
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Fussy eaters, for instance, are loaded into lorries.
explanation.definitionFit: They refuse meat, dairy, eggs and every other animal product.

clue.text: One sort of politician gave the queen an itemised record

parts.note: to feed someone information is to give it to them, so gave is fed
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth II
an itemised record is a list, and with the article it reads a list

explanation.surface: A politician handed the monarch a detailed inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of a system where states share power with a central government.

clue.text: The PM, very good and always completely sober

parts.note: pi is old British slang for pious, sanctimoniously good
TT stands for teetotal, never drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A prime minister praised as virtuous and never drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: William Pitt, father or son, each a British prime minister in the eighteenth century. The younger was a notoriously heavy drinker of port, which gives the surface its irony.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: two British prime ministers, the Elder and the Younger, bore this surname.

clue.text: Quiet bit should be audible

indicators.note: should be audible says the word for bit is to be taken as it is spoken

parts.note: a bit of something is a piece of it

explanation.surface: A soft passage of music ought still to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a noun: a bit of quiet is a spell of calm and stillness.

clue.text: Rodent seen round B&B, getting one to chatter

indicators.note: seen round says the rodent's letters are found on either side of the rest

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

indicators.note: getting adds the single letter after the pair of Bs

parts.note: B and B, without the ampersand, is two letter Bs
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A mouse spotted near a guest house sets someone gossiping.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is British slang from Cockney rhyming slang, where 'rabbit and pork' stands for talk. The animal itself is not a rodent, which adds to the tease.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: to talk on and on at length about nothing much.

clue.text: 'Leadership good for all to see' — one given to spin?

indicators.note: given to hands the single letter on to the final word, which follows it

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good, as on school reports
U is the British film certificate for universal, suitable for everyone to see
I is the Roman numeral for one
to spin round the floor is, loosely, to dance; the question mark admits the stretch

explanation.surface: A slogan praises open government, quoted by a publicity man.
explanation.walkthrough: U was the British cinema rating meaning anyone may watch. The surface paints a spin doctor; 'spin' is only whirling on a dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: direction and advice given by someone in charge.

clue.text: Garment to hang loose round short man

indicators.note: round says the word for hang loose goes on either side of the man's name

parts.note: something that sags hangs loosely
Ron is the short form of the man's name Ronald

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing draped baggily about a little fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short man' is not a small person but a shortened name, Ron for Ronald, and 'round' wraps SAG about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a length of cloth wrapped about the body, worn in South-East Asia.

clue.text: The church has actual food

indicators.note: has attaches the word for actual directly after the church's initials

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
something actual is real

explanation.surface: A parish puts on a proper meal.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: grain, or a breakfast dish made from it.
